To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) income-related inequality among the elderly is limited, but increases with age; (2) this increase with age is not due to the income concept, but rather to the presence of sample attrition and mortality.

(1) income-related inequality in self-reported ill-health is present in Belgium; (2) the inequality reduces significantly as soon one restricts the sample to the 65+; and (3) the findings are robust to the use of alternative measures of income.
(1) inequality in ill-health is very limited among the elderly; and (2), the difference between the 65+ and the 65− may be explained by differences in sample attrition and mortality.

the measurement of socio-economic differences in ill-health among elderly people.
